bullets.title: FOMC turns hawkish under Warsh: 9 dots project 2026 rate hike, core PCE raised to 3.3%
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural June FOMC meeting removed forward guidance, shortened the statement, and showed 9 of 18 participants penciling in at least one 2026 rate hike (6 expecting 2+). Median 2026 core PCE was revised sharply higher to 3.3% from 2.7%. Markets repriced ~36-40bp of hikes through year-end vs ~19bp pre-meeting; OIS now pricing a full hike by October. Morgan Stanley sees the inflation trajectory as slower than the SEP implies and holds a 'stay on hold' call, noting SEP forecasts were submitted pre-Hormuz.

bullets.title: US-Iran MOU signed; Hormuz reopening drives WTI down 10%+ on the week, Brent to ~$80
bullets.body: A framework agreement between the US and Iran was signed, immediately lifting the blockade on Iranian ports and enabling oil exports to resume. WTI fell ~10.6% on the week to below $77, with Goldman projecting 70% Gulf export recovery by month-end. JPMorgan estimates 80M+ barrels of stranded non-Iranian crude on VLCCs ready to transit at short notice, reinforcing a bearish near-term oil supply outlook. Lower oil is disinflatory, supporting dovish Fed reinterpretation and rotation into consumer discretionary, airlines, housing, and autos.

bullets.title: S&P 500 hits 11th weekly gain in 12; Nasdaq led by semis +7.3%, breadth at 3rd percentile
bullets.body: The S&P 500 ended the week +0.93%, Dow and Russell 2000 hit fresh record highs. Nasdaq outperformed at +2.43%, driven by memory/DRAM (+18%) and semis (+7.3%). Critically, only ~30% of stocks outperformed the index—3rd percentile breadth—as the AI momentum trade narrowed. JPMorgan and MS describe the tape as 'narrow AI rally' with levered ETF demand near record highs (~$20bn per 1% SPX move in short gamma).

bullets.title: Fed dot plot implies range-bound rates until 2027-28; Warsh signals communication reform
bullets.body: Warsh emphasized 'price stability' 13x vs. labor markets 3x and dropped forward guidance entirely—the shortest FOMC statement in years. He announced five task forces covering communications, balance sheet, data sources, productivity/jobs, and inflation framework. The long-run dot median moved to 3.2%, suggesting a sustainably higher neutral rate. 22V pegs the monthly core PCE breakeven at 0.21%; recent prints at ~0.36% raise the probability of actual tightening if trajectory doesn't improve.

bullets.title: AI capex estimates raised to $5.5T through 2030; MSFT flagged as ~$90-130B underfunded in FY27-28
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised total AI infrastructure capex estimates to $5.5T through 2030 (from $5.1T), with $4.1T debt-funded and LTCs averaging 85%+. Google and Amazon are aggressively pre-funding FY27-28 ramps (~$300-350B each), while MSFT is flagged as approximately one year behind on funding—the most likely source of new IG supply in 2H26. NVIDIA is separately raising $20-25B in IG bonds, its first debt issuance since 2021. Hyperscaler GPU rental at $50/watt (Google's reported GB300 deal) implies strong AI monetization and upward bias to cloud revenue estimates.

bullets.title: Memory/DRAM supercycle: DRAM ASPs +200% in 2026, MU up 15.5% on week; AAPL faces 'unavoidable' price hikes
bullets.body: Citi forecasts DRAM spot prices up 52% YTD and projects +200% ASP growth for full-year 2026 on data center demand and constrained supply—raising MU PT to $1,200 and WFE estimates to $145B/$200B/$250B in 2026/27/28. Apple CEO Tim Cook confirmed memory and storage costs are 'unsustainable,' citing hyperscalers locking up 50%+ of supply. Samsung's 2Q26 operating profit is expected to exceed W100T. MU reports June 24 (consensus $20.57 EPS / $35.56B revenue).

bullets.title: Accenture crashes 23% on booking miss, AI disintermediation fears; IT services sector reprices
bullets.body: ACN's F3Q revenue of $18.72B slightly missed; crucially, managed services book-to-bill fell below 1.0x for the first time since 2019, and FY26 growth guidance was narrowed to 3-4% (from 3-5%). Morgan Stanley downgraded to EW, cutting PT to $177 from $240. Multiple firms see negative read-across to Capgemini and CTSH. ACN's $4.175B acquisition of Dragos, runZero, and NetRise is seen as a pivot toward cybersecurity to offset organic growth headwinds.

bullets.title: INTC surges 10%+ on Trump-backed Apple chip partnership and 18A-P production milestone
bullets.body: Trump announced Apple agreed to work with Intel to design and manufacture chips in the US; Intel separately began risk production of its advanced 18A-P node (9% perf / 18% power improvement vs 18A). Analyst estimates peg the deal at ~5% of TSMC's Apple business, or $1-1.2B annually, and validate Intel's foundry strategy. Samsung is simultaneously fielding rising chip requests from Google, AMD, and Tesla amid TSMC capacity constraints.

bullets.title: Software sector in pain: IGV -14.2% YTD, ACN miss fuels AI-disintermediation narrative
bullets.body: The IGV software ETF is down 14.2% YTD vs S&P +10.1%. CRM fell for 13 consecutive days (longest streak on record), INTU was downgraded to hold at Stifel, and ADBE is at 52-week lows. Enterprise AI adoption is shifting toward consumption-based pricing and token optimization ('token-minimizing'), pressuring seat-based SaaS. MSFT is considering hosting DeepSeek as a cheaper Copilot option. KeyBanc CIO survey indicates 34.5% of CIOs plan to reduce spend with legacy software vendors in favor of AI-native solutions.

bullets.title: Enterprise AI cost pressure intensifies: Uber, Walmart, AT&T cap AI usage; token-minimizing replaces token-maxxing
bullets.body: Multiple large enterprises have hit or capped AI budgets mid-year: Uber exhausted its 2026 AI budget in four months, Walmart capped AI tool usage, and AT&T is curtailing employee access. MSFT CEO Nadella publicly urged employees to avoid frontier models for non-frontier tasks. Median AI spend per employee is $11.38/month but top 1% spend ~$7,500/month. The shift from experimentation to cost-governed deployment is compressing near-term enterprise software revenue upside.

bullets.title: HDD cycle elongates: WDC target raised to $650, STX to $1,035 on $25-30/TB pricing trajectory
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Erik Woodring raised WDC PT to $650 and STX PT to $1,035 after Asia checks confirm HDD shortages through at least CY28. Current nearline HDD pricing is below $15/TB; vendors are targeting $25-30/TB over 2-3 years, implying base-case FY28 EPS ~70% above consensus. Hyperscalers are signing LTAs through 2032 and prioritizing storage over compute in some capex plans.

bullets.title: FOX acquires Roku for $160/share ($22B EV); FOXA down 17%, ROKU receives mass downgrades
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku at $160/share (60% cash, 40% stock), creating the third-largest US TV player by viewership with $23B revenue and ~8% EBITDA CAGR. The deal targets $400M run-rate cost synergies and FCF accretion by year 2. ROKU was downgraded to neutral/hold by 8+ analysts on deal announcement. FOX fell ~17% as investors digest $12B new debt and ~38% dilution, though UBS and Citi frame the valuation impact as an overreaction.

bullets.title: BoJ hiked 25bp to 1.0%; ECB and BoE hold with tightening biases intact
bullets.body: Bank of Japan raised policy rate to 1% (7-1 vote), a 31-year high, with the next hike expected in October. The BoE held 7-2 with Green and Pill dissenting hawkishly for a 25bp hike; JPM pushed its BoE hike call from July to November after UK CPI came in at 2.8% vs a 3.3% forecast. JPM expects one more ECB hike in September despite the Iran deal lowering energy prices, as core inflation is tracking 2.5%+ through early 2027.

bullets.title: Hedge fund gross leverage at 98th percentile; seasonal peak expected mid-June before summer decline
bullets.body: JPMorgan prime data shows HF gross leverage hit 98th percentile, with the largest May increase in history (+22% vs 6% avg) and a sizable June increase (+18% vs 10% avg). Historically, gross leverage peaks around mid-June options expiry and declines through late July. Semis represent 32% of hedge fund net leverage vs 5% in 2023. Nearly 20% of funds have <10% AI exposure despite the theme at record positioning levels—creating both 'AI FOMO' and potential VaR shock dynamics.

bullets.title: UBS raises MSCI AC World target to 1,200; JPM tactically bullish; Wells Fargo lifts S&P to 7,950
bullets.body: UBS upgraded its MSCI AC World year-end target to 1,200 from 1,120 on Middle East settlement. JPMorgan flipped to Tactically Bullish following the Iran deal but warned the 'everything rally' historically fades into concentrated Tech leadership. Wells Fargo raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,950 from 7,300. Piper Sandler targets 8,450 on 21.5x $393 2027 EPS, noting earnings growth (not multiple expansion) is driving the market with P/E expansion limited unless rates fall sustainably.

bullets.title: FERC unanimously approves Trump plan to accelerate AI data center grid connections
bullets.body: FERC voted unanimously to allow large loads like AI data centers to connect to the grid in a 'timely and orderly manner,' with data centers required to fund incremental infrastructure upgrades. PUCT separately approved a batch interconnection process for ERCOT covering 35 GW of baseload and 65 GW under study. These approvals benefit IPPs (TLN, VST, CEG) and unlock PJM contracting that had been stalled.

bullets.title: Retail sector: May retail sales +0.9% m/m beat; AI-referred traffic +138% YoY, converts 54% better
bullets.body: May retail sales rose 0.9% m/m (consensus 0.6%), with control group up 0.7%; 2Q real consumption tracking raised to ~2.9% q/q (MS). Adobe data shows AI-referred US retail visits surged 138% YoY in May 2026 (up 1,324% since October 2024), with AI-sourced shoppers spending 54% more per visit and browsing 23% more pages. Despite overall resilience, retail traffic data (Citi, KeyBanc) shows sequential deceleration across most categories into 2Q.

bullets.title: Qualcomm reportedly in $8-10B Tenstorrent acquisition talks; AMD-Rackspace 30MW AI compute deal signed
bullets.body: Qualcomm is in advanced discussions to acquire RISC-V AI accelerator startup Tenstorrent (led by ex-AMD Zen architect Jim Keller) for $8-10B. Separately, AMD signed a definitive agreement with Rackspace for phased deployment of 30 MW of AMD-based AI compute from late 2026-2028. These moves signal broad semiconductor-ecosystem competition intensifying beyond NVIDIA.

bullets.title: Capital markets activity surging: M&A +64% YoY, equity issuance +117%, IPOs +415% in 2Q
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's deal dashboard shows 2Q26 capital markets activity is tracking sharply higher year-over-year across all categories. IPO volumes are up 415%, equity issuance up 117% (North America +234%), and annualized M&A volume up 64% with sponsor trends flipping to positive. This is a broad-based acceleration with completed M&A up 27%, pointing to an improving confidence and liquidity backdrop.

bullets.title: BoJ hike, dollar index +1.1%, curve flattening: 2Y yield +9bp, 30Y -7bp on the week
bullets.body: The Treasury curve flattened meaningfully with 2-year yields rising 9bp to ~4.20% on the hawkish Fed while the 30-year fell 7bp to ~4.90% as stranded supply from the Hormuz reopening provided disinflation signals. JPMorgan maintains 10s/30s flatteners. Foreign investors were net buyers of $50.5B in Treasuries in April (highest since November 2025), though JPM revised full-year foreign demand down to $450B from $500B. Gold edged up 0.2% on the week.
